We are a Saudi-based AI & Digital Transformation Agency building end-to-end digital systems, WhatsApp AI engines, process automations, and CRM integrations for fast-growing businesses in the Arab world and MENA region.

We are looking for a Hands-on AI & Operations Lead to help us build a fully AI-First operational hub. This is not a traditional PM role — we need a system builder, an automation architect, and a problem solver who loves turning complex operational bottlenecks into sleek, automated n8n & Make.com workflows.

What You’ll Be Building & Managing

  • AI-First Operations: Designing and deploying scalable workflows using n8n, LLM APIs (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini), and custom webhooks to eliminate repetitive internal tasks.

  • WhatsApp AI Automations: Building advanced WhatsApp Business API flows integrated with CRMs and AI agents for client and internal operations.

Requirements & Tech Stack

  • Expertise in n8n & Make.com: Advanced workflow design, self-hosting/deployment concepts, custom Webhooks, JSON parsing, JS/Python code nodes, Error handling, and API calls.

  • Daily hands-on AI usage: Deep integration experience with LLM APIs (ChatGPT/OpenAI, Claude, Gemini) and AI Agents.

  • PM & Ops Experience: Proven background leading digital projects or operational teams inside a startup or digital agency.

  • Tooling: Proficient in Google Workspace, ClickUp/Asana/Notion, WhatsApp Business API integrations, and modern PM tools.

  • Mindset: Extreme ownership, self-driven, and obsessed with system scalability and clean workflow architecture.

Perks & Contract Details

  • Type: Long-term, ongoing renewable contract (Project/Contract-based).

  • Location: 100% Remote.

  • Hours: Flexible hours

  • Growth: High potential to step into a core leadership role as the agency scales.

How to Apply

Please drop a reply or private message with:

  1. A brief introduction & your background in automation/operations (mention any experience with Middle East / GCC projects).

  2. Your daily AI & Automation stack (e.g., n8n nodes, Make scenarios, tools, models).

  3. Showcase: 1–2 real-world complex automation workflows you’ve built in n8n or Make.com (screenshots, Loom videos, or architecture descriptions are highly welcome!).

  4. Your weekly hourly availability and time zone.

  5. What’s the biggest automation or AI system you’ve managed from scratch?

Hello,

I saw your post about building an AI-first operations hub, and the WhatsApp automation side of it is close to the work I do.

WhatsApp AI at agency scale fails for a consistent reason. The first ten builds go well, and then delivery becomes the constraint rather than sales. Every new client is a fresh number, a fresh CRM and a fresh set of flows, and if each one is hand-built, the tenth client costs the same as the first and the margin goes. So the first thing worth solving is making a client deployment repeatable, not clever: a templated flow set, a standard way of wiring the CRM, and a checklist that catches connection problems before the client does.

On the technical shape, from doing this work:

- n8n as the orchestration spine, because your team and your clients can see and edit what is happening. In an agency that matters more than in a single company, since handover is constant.

- LLM abstraction from day one. OpenAI, Claude and Gemini behind one step, so moving a client to a different model is a config change rather than a rebuild.

- WhatsApp Business API with the handoff solved properly. The bot has to yield to a human cleanly and take the conversation back, which needs a real state model rather than a pause flag.

- Error handling and run visibility as a default. When a client’s automation stops silently, that becomes your support ticket, and you do not want to hear about it from them.

Happy to go deeper on any of it, or to talk about how the ops lead role and a build subcontract might fit together.

- n8n as the orchestration spine, because your team and your clients can see and edit what is happening. In an agency that matters more than in a single company, since handover is constant.

- LLM abstraction from day one. OpenAI, Claude and Gemini behind one step, so moving a client to a different model is a config change rather than a rebuild.

- WhatsApp Business API with the handoff solved properly. The bot has to yield to a human cleanly and take the conversation back, which needs a real state model rather than a pause flag.

- Error handling and run visibility as a default. When a client’s automation stops silently, that becomes your support ticket, and you do not want to hear about it from them.
